opening_message:
Ticket 1: Eric Woods (employee ID E019) requests write access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E019.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Engineer (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Eric Woods (E019) is a full-time Engineer. Requested write access to Payroll. Full-time employees may have up to write; admin requires owning role (Payroll Specialist), which Engineer is not. Recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - role: Engineer (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security record: E019 is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors may have read, or write only with advanced training. Requested write to Payroll, so recommend read (maximum).
reason: Eric Woods (E019) requested write access to Payroll. The team notes conflict on employment type: the HR note lists full-time, while the Security note (verified in their own database) lists contractor with basic security training. Under the contractor policy, write requires advanced security training; with only basic training, the maximum allowed is read. Given the conflicting employment records, I apply the more restrictive, least-privilege interpretation, so the maximum is read and the granted level is read.
